summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and a history of gastritis was admitted for sudden-onset sharp left-sided chest pain that radiated to the epigastrium and was associated with right upper quadrant abdominal pain. Initial concern for cardiac ischemia was ruled out with stable troponins and unchanged EKG. Abdominal pain was evaluated with a liver/gallbladder ultrasound, which showed stable cholelithiasis without cholecystitis. The pain was attributed to gastritis, given its post-prandial nature and history of prior gastritis. Hyperkalemia (K+ 6.3) improved with kayexalate and subsequent hemodialysis. The patient's symptoms improved, Nexium was increased to twice daily, and he was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged in gastroenterology.
problems: Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, without mention of hemorrhage
Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
Calculus of gallbladder without mention of cholecystitis, without mention of obstruction
